title: Learning in Rio how well Lester was known after his death
summary: Arriving in Rio in 1960 three months after Lester died, Lee was interviewed about his brother and was moved by his fame abroad.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Do you remember what year that was?

Uh huh. Let's see, I think it was '59. Because we went to South America in '60, and that's when Lester passed, in '60. And the people -- that's why I said about music -- when we got to Rio, all these people met us at the airport, and Lester had been deceased for about 3 months, and I was just getting back to myself where I could talk about it, and here at this airport, this jazz club that they have over there -- they met me and interviewed me and started talking about Lester and they just really broke me up all over again.

Because, you know, what really broke me up was the idea that many miles from the USA, and they still knew my brother, and you know, they just idolized him; all the records, everything. And it's kind of -- it's an education for you because you just do not imagine that people know about you ... as I think I told you about when we first went to England.
